previous_description: Modular, deployable, and replaceable part of a system
definition: An active structural application element that encapsulates a cohesive set of application behaviour and data behind its interfaces and can be built, deployed, or replaced as a unit, such as a service, module, package, or dependency-injected class with its own responsibility. It is the thing that performs behaviour, not the behaviour itself.

distinguish_from.when: the symbol is a unit of behaviour, such as a method, function, or handler body, that a component performs, rather than the structural unit that owns that behaviour
the symbol is only the access point through which a component's services are reached, such as a controller endpoint set, client stub, or exported port, rather than the implementing unit
the symbol represents a grouping of several components that work together, such as a system-of-services or a composite deployment, rather than a single replaceable unit
the symbol is a passive data structure, such as a DTO, record, or entity without behaviour of its own, that components read or write

code_evidence: a module, package, or service directory with its own build manifest or deployment descriptor (package.json, pom.xml, go.mod, Dockerfile, Kubernetes Deployment)
a class annotated or registered as a managed component in a DI container (@Component, @Service, @Injectable, Module providers) whose instances are injected into other classes
an entry in docker-compose, Helm charts, or an architecture/service catalogue (e.g. Backstage catalog-info.yaml) naming the unit as a separately deployable service or library

attribute_descriptions.name: documentation
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text narrative describing the component's responsibility, boundaries, and notable dependencies. Set it whenever the component's name alone does not convey what it owns or why it exists.

notes: The attribute named 'type' collides with the element-type concept and mixes two axes: ownership (internal/external) and style (service-component), with 'generic' as a catch-all. Consider splitting it into 'sourcing' and 'kind'. Granularity is unclear: are plain classes components or should only deployables qualify? The self 'uses' relationship is listed twice.
